questions.question: What is the core quality invariant for an interactive meeting under congestion?
options: Protect intelligible audio and continuity before maximum video detail
Keep every gallery tile in HD even if audio breaks
Wait for analytics acknowledgement before forwarding packets
Move every participant after one high-latency sample
questions.explanation: Conversation depends on timely, intelligible audio. Resolution, frame rate, and gallery size should degrade before audio or the meeting connection.

questions.question: In the balanced example, what is the approximate downlink per receiver for one 0.9 Mbps speaker stream, six 0.12 Mbps thumbnails, and three 0.04 Mbps audio streams?
options: 1.74 Mbps
0.90 Mbps
2.70 Mbps
10.44 Mbps
questions.explanation: The receiver budget is 0.9 + (6 x 0.12) + (3 x 0.04) = 1.74 Mbps.

questions.question: Why can SFU outbound bandwidth dominate its inbound bandwidth?
options: Each published stream can be forwarded in a different subscription mix to many receivers
The SFU stores every meeting forever
Every participant uploads one copy per database replica
The control plane re-encodes all packets
questions.explanation: The SFU receives each publisher once but fans selected streams and layers out to many participant-specific subscriptions.

questions.question: What should happen after a single SFU crashes?
options: Issue a newer standby assignment, reconnect clients, republish tracks, and rebuild subscriptions
Assume all ephemeral forwarding state survived
Delete the meeting and require a new meeting ID
Wait for the analytics warehouse to reconstruct packets
questions.explanation: Meeting identity can survive, but the failed SFU's live transport and subscription state must be rebuilt on healthy capacity.

questions.question: Why does a quality controller use hysteresis?
options: To degrade on sustained bad evidence but require more good evidence before upgrading
To make every participant use the same layer
To eliminate the need for packet-loss measurement
To maximize route changes during transient jitter
questions.explanation: Different degrade and recovery thresholds prevent quality from oscillating when measurements briefly cross one boundary.

questions.question: What is the expected trade-off when a regional outage moves participants to a recovery region?
options: Meeting identity can continue, but reconnect time and network latency may rise, so video should start conservatively
Latency must fall because every failover route is shorter
No client transport needs to reconnect
Authorization should be skipped to speed recovery
questions.explanation: Cross-region recovery preserves the meeting contract, but a longer route and transport rebuild can temporarily reduce quality.

questions.question: Why keep meeting control separate from the media forwarding path?
options: Established media can continue through bounded control-plane trouble without a database lookup per packet
Media packets never need authorization
The SFU should own billing and scheduling
Control state is larger than all video traffic
questions.explanation: The control plane authorizes and assigns the route, while the latency-sensitive media plane forwards and adapts packets locally.
